location.section: Sign-Off and Handoff Readiness

findings.finding: The PRD explicitly records an unmet formal upstream readiness condition: BRD v0.15.0 is unsigned and lacks current approved upstream quality evidence. Approved exercise assumptions disposition company discovery for exercise design but do not supply that governed evidence.
findings.recommendation: Preserve this declared upstream governance limitation and the exact BRD revision. Return the bounded exercise review for owner acceptance without fabricating a handoff, company signatures or upstream quality approval; obtain governed upstream evidence only for the corresponding governed adoption route.

location.section: Functional Requirements; Acceptance Criteria; Independently reportable review checks

findings.finding: Several parent requirements combine independently implementable behaviors; FR-014 bundles service intake, redress, accessible contact, representative authority, measure decisions, withdrawal and appointment outcomes. AC-017/037 and the existing subcheck table do not fully decompose that bundle into individually identifiable obligations and outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Retain existing parent IDs as traceability anchors, but decompose their independent obligations into canonical atomic requirements and criteria. Start with FR-014/AC-017/037, then apply the same audit to return/history/ invalidation, provider delivery and quality/handover bundles; preserve reciprocal links and publish one separately reported oracle per obligation.

location.section: Staff data trust and control; Owner direction for pilot readiness; Simplicity and adoption requirements

findings.finding: TR/DH/PR/SA tables continue to express additional MVP or pilot obligations outside the declared FR/AC/NFR/CON requirement namespaces without a complete canonical mapping or an unambiguous non-normative disposition. SA-005 also promises any workbook while FR-029 limits import to declared exercise structures, and SA-008 cites the hazard constraint CON-006 for resident decision rights.
findings.recommendation: Mark supplementary rows explicitly as non-normative source/proposal aliases with release disposition, or map each adopted obligation to canonical requirements and ACs. Qualify SA-005 to the declared supported workbook contract and correct SA-008 to CON-003/FR-014/FR-044; qualify upstream RULE references so they are not mistaken for local requirement IDs.

location.section: Exercise Acceptance Contract / Forecast, Dashboard and Financial Oracles

findings.finding: The stated six central handovers is consistent with a two-stage pipeline only if installation and independent QA/handover can operate concurrently with sufficient separately declared stage capacity; the text does not explicitly distinguish that from one shared two-homes/week resource pool. EXA-009 also approves one/two-week duration sensitivity, but this section explicitly enumerates only the capacity one/three sensitivity.
findings.recommendation: State the resource pool and concurrency rule for each stage and publish the independently authored central weekly handover oracle, preserving the approved six-home week-four target. Explicitly require the approved two-week stage-duration sensitivity alongside the six frozen scenarios, with its independently authored schedule and stated capacity semantics.

location.section: Exercise Acceptance Contract; Independently reportable review checks; Four-Week Evidence Plan

findings.finding: The exercise contract distinguishes Not run and Blocked from Pass, but the subcheck instructions allow only pass/fail/not-applicable and call unimplemented required checks failures. The evidence plan then introduces Observed as an outcome without defining its relationship to pass/fail.
findings.recommendation: Use one result vocabulary throughout: Pass, Fail, Not run, Blocked and Not applicable, with evidence recorded separately as observations. Required checks that remain unexecuted cannot pass acceptance, but should not be misreported as executed test failures; require explicit reasons and versioned applicability for exclusions.

location.section: Product Context; Workflow Coverage; Functional Requirements

findings.finding: Canonical requirements address the documented shared-case, evidence, coordination, authority and reporting needs. AI assistance is tied to bounded tasks and comparative learning rather than assumed automation benefits.

location.section: Product boundary; Component Contracts; Design Decisions and Options Gate

findings.finding: One product is justified by shared state, permissions, evidence and handoffs; workflow modules remain delivery increments. DD-001 through DD-008 distinguish proposed design choices from production selection, procurement approval and imposed constraints.

location.section: Functional Requirements; Exercise Acceptance Contract; Open Questions

findings.finding: Current exercise scope, T0, external-action prohibitions, mandatory unknown handling and human decision boundaries are explicit enough for downstream use. Local forecast and reporting ambiguities are separately identified in req-qual-004/005 rather than treated as absent requirements.

location.section: Exercise Baseline Authority; Exercise Acceptance Contract; Sign-Off and Handoff Readiness

findings.finding: The draft supplies exercise role accountability, scoped quantitative targets, source/form contracts, failure handling, financial fixtures and an evidence plan. All sixteen OQs have documented exercise dispositions; future company research and actual inference prerequisites are not represented as answered facts.

location.section: Exercise Baseline Authority; Performance, Scale, Recovery and Budget; Four-Week Evidence Plan

findings.finding: The four-week exercise is bounded by a lean local/minimal-cloud option, reusable contracts, explicit spending allocations and separate core/scale workloads. Real access, API, processing and price verification remains a specific execution prerequisite, not assumed feasibility evidence.

location.section: Exercise Acceptance Contract; Acceptance Criteria; Independently reportable review checks

findings.finding: Objective inspection and test methods are specified for critical controls, recovery, performance, chart reconciliation, field disposition and comparisons. AC-047 now has independent extraction subchecks and AC-051 requires exact fixture-owned direct/transitive invalidation sets.

location.section: Exercise Baseline Authority; Form Extraction and Assisted Filling; Sign-Off and Handoff Readiness

findings.finding: The current draft faithfully distinguishes approved exercise assumptions, pending final owner acceptance, unexecuted targets and operational authority. Historical form-route and application/claim isolation defects are corrected; the bounded forecast-fidelity omission is separately recorded.

location.section: Non-Functional Requirements; Observability and SLO Measurement Method; Exercise Acceptance Contract

findings.finding: All ten categories are present: NFR-002 covers performance and scaling, NFR-006 recovery, NFR-003 security, NFR-005 privacy, NFR-011 operability, NFR-004/011 telemetry, NFR-001 accessibility, NFR-008 exchange contracts with the declared import/interface boundary, and NFR-010 portability. Presence does not establish implementation effectiveness or conformance.

location.section: Product Goals

findings.finding: All four goals have bounded exercise populations, quantitative criteria or comparators, plausible scoped delivery with recorded risks, relevance and a T0+4-week deadline. GOAL-004 accepts measured lack of benefit as a learning outcome without activating a failing task or waiving real inference.

location.section: Functional Requirements; Acceptance Criteria; Traceability Matrix

findings.finding: All 44 FR definitions have valid reciprocal links to the 54 AC definitions, and the FR-to-AC matrix matches both tables. Every FR links to at least one of four valid goals; the goal matrix matches the FR goal column, and canonical FR/AC/NFR/CON/GOAL/DD definitions have valid suffixes without duplicate definitions or numbering gaps.

location.section: Constraints

findings.finding: CON-001 identifies owner/upstream scope as its imposing source, names the non-production/data boundary and prohibits live authority and integrations. It is an imposed scope constraint, not desired functionality.

location.section: Constraints

findings.finding: CON-002 identifies the upstream operating model and the retained source-system authority boundary. Separate approval is required to change that integration/authority constraint.

location.section: Constraints

findings.finding: CON-003 cites the case and upstream authority model, names the affected human decision owners and forbids substitution by agents or UI actions. It is a decision-rights constraint distinct from permission implementation.

location.section: Constraints

findings.finding: CON-004 identifies owner/addendum governance as its source and prohibits inferred production, platform or procurement approval. DD-001 remains a proposed design baseline rather than a disguised imposed architecture.

location.section: Constraints

findings.finding: CON-005 imposes an evidence/estate boundary from the owner's estate statement: no dependency on unverified installed services. The storage fallback is correctly kept separate as a design option.

location.section: Constraints

findings.finding: CON-006 names the upstream hazard duty and retained service authority, with an explicit prohibition on delay, clock manipulation, classification and closure. It is a safety/authority boundary rather than a negotiable response-time NFR.

location.section: Constraints

findings.finding: CON-007 identifies upstream authority/separation rules, the bulk-action boundary and non-negotiable independent authorization. FR-007 provides enforcement behavior without changing the constraint's classification.

location.section: Constraints

findings.finding: CON-008 identifies upstream evidence controls and the reporting boundary: forecasts cannot be represented as guarantees or commitments. Forecast quality and reproduction remain separately expressed under NFR-007.

smart_product_goals.statement: By T0+4 weeks, each of the eleven profile scripts shall identify its permitted work, blocker, evidence, owner and next action without an unexplained dead-end or permission breach.
By T0+4 weeks, demonstrate the nine connected workflows, including one same-home journey with an EPC conflict, correction, independent handover and financial closure.
By T0+4 weeks, produce reconciled cohort dashboards and a reproducible four-week scenario forecast.
By T0+4 weeks, establish task-level value or lack of value using real Foundry inference and paired manual/parser comparisons without weakening controls.

notes:
Scope: independent current full PRD review, not an amendment-only review.
Taxonomy: FR/AC/NFR/CON; GOAL and DD are adjacent namespaces.
Inventory: 44 FRs, 54 ACs, 13 NFRs, 8 CONs, 4 GOALs, 8 DDs,
16 future operational OQs, and zero unanswered exercise OQs.

Read evidence: current PRD v0.12.0; owner-approved addendum baseline
including EXA-001..016, numeric targets and evidence plan; BRD v0.15.0;
current PRD state; original v0.11.0 paired reports and historical
challenge disposition. Historical findings were reassessed, not inherited
as current defects. No historical report was altered.

Rubric: canonical requirements-author spec_version 1.1, exposed under
the contracts' combined requirements-quality bundle name. Both payload
contracts were read before scoring, together with shared score anchors,
SMART and NIST presence references.

SMART achievability is a plausibility judgement under the documented
exercise constraints, not successful access, implementation or delivery.
T0 is final acceptance of the reviewed baseline, not assumption approval.
Human exercise-label adjudication is later engineering evidence; it is
not company approval or direct user research.

Numeric checks: 30+30+60 families = 120; 60 held-out packs x 12 fields =
720 dispositions. Related families stay within one split; unresolved
labels require counted exclusions and restored coverage. Overall field
disposition accuracy includes required abstention; selected-field accuracy
and answerable-subset coverage are separate. Macro-F1, critical-category
counts and finite-suite zero-failure limitations are explicit.
Twelve counterbalanced pack pairs compare full net effort, not token price.

Finance: GBP 18,000 contractor milestones reconcile to 3,600/12,600/1,800.
Base 20,000 includes contractor 18,000 plus internal allocation 2,000;
contingency 2,000 produces envelope 22,000. Eligible 16,000 and grant
min(7,500, 50%) produce provider base 12,500 and gross pre-receipt exposure
20,000. These are fictional fixtures, not real entitlement or company finance.
USD 450/month includes attributable existing charges and accrued liabilities;
allocations sum to 450 and warn/pause thresholds are 360/405. Labour is
reported separately; budget alerts alone are not a hard spending cap.

Forecast: independent constructed event/capacity schedules, exact reruns,
weekly cumulative MAE and week-four error are required. Unknown/abstained
predictions cannot be counted as zero-error results. The six-home central
target is not rejected; stage resource semantics and the approved duration
sensitivity need the precision identified in req-qual-004.

Safety and authority: candidate-only/no-match, preserved conflicts,
protected declarations/signatures/certifications/resident decisions,
individual required-field review, API permissions, no self-approval,
independent handoff acceptance/update ownership and human-first hazard
triage are explicit. Negative or failed models cannot suppress triage,
infer consent or change ranking. Reviewed export, application submission,
award, claim and cash remain distinct.

Decision 1 and generative Foundry success calls are essential demonstration
evidence. Optional task activation and simpler fallback do not waive that
evidence requirement. Actual subscription/API/access/processing/cost checks
remain execution prerequisites; this review did not run them or authorize
spend/deployment. No benefit, model-quality, accessibility-conformance or
real user-validation assertion is made.

Ancillary obligations are excluded from the canonical 44-FR denominator
until adopted or dispositioned explicitly. Link coverage is not atomicity,
behavioral completeness or passing acceptance evidence.

Timestamp uses the caller-supplied invocation timestamp; no separate
completion clock was available. Findings were checked against contract
keys, enumerations, counts and score ranges manually. No files were written.
